questions.question: The formation of Cyclone 'Hamoon' in October 2023, emerging soon after 'Tej', occurred in which sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bay of Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cyclone 'Hamoon' formed in October 2023 over the **Bay of Bengal**, shortly after Cyclone 'Tej', which developed in the Arabian Sea.
 
• The Bay of Bengal is known for generating cyclones during the post-monsoon season (October-November), making it a hotspot for tropical storms.
 
• 'Hamoon' followed typical cyclonic development patterns influenced by low-pressure systems, warm sea surface temperatures, and favorable atmospheric conditions.
 
• Cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal generally impact the eastern coastal states of India, such as Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal, as well as Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
• The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) tracks and monitors cyclonic systems in the Bay of Bengal to provide timely warnings and mitigate disaster risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arabian Sea**

 
 
• The Arabian Sea is another region prone to cyclonic activities, especially during the pre-monsoon and post-monsoon seasons.
 
• Cyclone 'Tej', which preceded 'Hamoon', formed in the Arabian Sea and primarily affected Yemen and Oman.
 
 
 
• **Andaman Sea**
 
 
• The Andaman Sea lies to the southeast of the Bay of Bengal and is less significant in terms of cyclonic activity compared to the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.
 
• It plays a role in the early stages of cyclone formation before systems move into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Warm sea surface temperatures and monsoonal wind currents occasionally contribute to the development of low-pressure areas in the Andaman Sea.
 
 
 
• **South China Sea**
 
 
• The South China Sea is a region known for typhoon formation rather than cyclones.
 
• Tropical storms and typhoons in this area primarily affect countries like Vietnam, the Philippines, and China.
 
• While it does not directly contribute to cyclonic activity in the Indian subcontinent, weather systems from the South China Sea can sometimes influence the Bay of Bengal indirectly.

questions.question: The significant Chhayavaad work 'Kamayani', recognized for its profound philosophical, emotional, and symbolic literary expression in early 20th-century Hindi poetry, was authored by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaishankar Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kamayani** is one of the most celebrated works of Hindi literature, written by **Jaishankar Prasad**, a prominent figure in the Chhayavaad literary movement.
 
• The poem explores deep philosophical themes, blending **human emotions with symbolic representations of nature, divinity, and self-realization**.
 
• Kamayani is known for its allegorical depiction of **mind (Manu) and heart (Shraddha)**, representing the intellectual and emotional aspects of human existence.
 
• This masterpiece is considered a hallmark of **Chhayavaad**, a Hindi literary movement that emphasized romanticism, mysticism, and the beauty of nature.
 
• Jaishankar Prasad's contribution to Hindi literature extended beyond poetry, as he also excelled in drama, prose, and fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sumitranandan Pant:**

 
 
• Sumitranandan Pant was a leading poet of the Chhayavaad era in Hindi literature.
 
• He is known for his works that celebrate nature and human emotions, often inspired by romanticism.
 
• Some of his famous works include **"Pallav"**, **"Gunjan"**, and **"Ritugeet"**.
 
• He received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** and the **Padma Bhushan** for his contributions to Hindi poetry.
 
 
 
• **Harivansh Rai Bachchan:**
 
 
• Harivansh Rai Bachchan was a renowned Hindi poet best known for his work **"Madhushala"**.
 
• His poetry focused on themes of existentialism, human struggle, and the beauty of life.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** for his contributions to Indian literature.
 
• Although he was not a key figure in Chhayavaad, his works have left a lasting impact on modern Hindi poetry.
 
 
 
• **Makhanlal Chaturvedi:**
 
 
• Makhanlal Chaturvedi was a noted poet, writer, and journalist, often associated with the **Indian freedom struggle**.
 
• His poetry reflects patriotism, human values, and social issues.
 
• His famous work **"Himkanti"** earned him the first **Sahitya Akademi Award** in Hindi literature.
 
• Although he was not directly linked to Chhayavaad, his writings hold a significant place in Hindi literature.
 
 
 
• **Chhayavaad:**
 
 
• Chhayavaad is a literary movement in Hindi poetry that emerged in the early 20th century.
 
• It is characterized by romanticism, the glorification of nature, mysticism, and the exploration of human emotions.
 
• Prominent poets of this movement include **Jaishankar Prasad**, **Sumitranandan Pant**, **Suryakant Tripathi Nirala**, and **Mahadevi Verma**.
 
• The movement was instrumental in shaping modern Hindi literature and establishing Hindi poetry as a significant cultural force.

questions.question: The 'Buland Darwaza' (Gate of Magnificence) at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate ____.

The correct answer is __**His victory over Gujarat**__.

__
 
• The Buland Darwaza, also known as the "Gate of Magnificence," is one of the most iconic architectural achievements of Emperor Akbar.
 
• It was constructed in 1601 AD at Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh, to commemorate Akbar's victory over Gujarat in 1573.
 
• This grand gateway stands as the main entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri and is a symbol of Mughal architectural brilliance.
 
• The Buland Darwaza is 40 meters high and 15 meters wide, making it one of the tallest gateways in the world.
 
• The inscriptions on the gateway reflect Akbar's secular outlook and his emphasis on religious tolerance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: His coronation ceremony**

 
 
• Akbar was crowned as the Mughal Emperor at the tender age of 13 in 1556 after the death of his father, Humayun.
 
• His coronation took place at Kalanaur, Punjab, and not at Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• There is no historical evidence suggesting that the Buland Darwaza was constructed to commemorate this event.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: The promulgation of Din-i-Ilahi**
 
 
• Din-i-Ilahi, or "Religion of God," was a syncretic religious movement introduced by Akbar in 1582.
 
• It aimed to blend elements of various religions, including Hinduism, Islam, Jainism, and Christianity, to promote unity and tolerance.
 
• While it was an important initiative of Akbar, the Buland Darwaza was not built in connection with this event.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The completion of Fatehpur Sikri as his capital**
 
 
• Fatehpur Sikri served as Akbar's capital from 1571 to 1585 and is renowned for its architectural marvels.
 
• The city was abandoned due to water scarcity, but the Buland Darwaza was constructed much later in 1601.
 
• Therefore, it was not related to the completion of Fatehpur Sikri as the capital.

questions.question: Which of the following powers is not vested in the Governor under the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diplomatic power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Indian Constitution, the Governor does not have **diplomatic powers**, as these powers are vested exclusively in the President of India.
 
• Diplomatic powers involve conducting foreign relations, appointing ambassadors, and representing the nation in international matters, which fall under the purview of the Central Government.
 
• The President, as the head of state, exercises diplomatic powers like entering into treaties and agreements, accrediting ambassadors, and receiving foreign dignitaries.
 
• The Governor's role is limited to the administration of the state and does not extend to matters concerning foreign diplomacy or international relations.
 
• Diplomatic powers are part of the Union List under Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution, which is handled solely by the central government, ensuring uniformity in foreign policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative powers:**

 
 
• The Governor acts as the executive head of the state and exercises administrative powers on behalf of the state government.
 
• He/she appoints the Chief Minister, other ministers, and state officials as per constitutional provisions.
 
• Administrative powers also include ensuring the implementation of constitutional provisions and maintaining law and order within the state.
 
 
 
• **Ordinance-making powers:**
 
 
• The Governor has the authority to issue ordinances under Article 213 of the Constitution when the state legislature is not in session and immediate legislative action is required.
 
• Ordinances have the same force and effect as laws passed by the legislature but must be approved by the legislature within six weeks of reassembly.
 
• This power is an important legislative function exercised by the Governor in exceptional circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Pardoning powers:**
 
 
• The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment under Article 161 of the Constitution for offenses against laws relating to matters under the state’s executive power.
 
• However, pardoning powers differ from those of the President, as the President can pardon offenses against Union laws and death sentences.
 
• The Governor’s pardoning powers are limited to state laws and do not extend to death sentences or offenses under central laws.

questions.question: The 'Battle of Haldighati' (1576) was fought between the Mughal army led by Man Singh and ______.

• The 'Battle of Haldighati' was fought on 18 June 1576 between the Mughal forces led by Raja Man Singh I of Amber and the forces of Maharana Pratap, the ruler of Mewar.
 
• This battle was a significant event in Indian history, showcasing Maharana Pratap's resistance against the mighty Mughal empire led by Emperor Akbar.
 
• Although the battle did not result in a decisive victory for either side, it demonstrated Maharana Pratap's valiant efforts to protect Mewar's sovereignty and independence.

• Maharana Pratap's loyal horse, Chetak, is remembered for his bravery during the battle, as he saved the Maharana's life but succumbed to injuries later.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ibrahim Lodi**

 
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty, which ruled the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He was defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, which marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• The battle ended the rule of the Delhi Sultanate and ushered in a new era of Mughal dominance in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Rani Durgavati**
 
 
• Rani Durgavati was the queen of Gondwana and a symbol of bravery and resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
• She is remembered for her valiant fight against Mughal forces led by Asaf Khan in 1564. She chose to sacrifice her life rather than surrender.
 
• Her courage and sacrifice are celebrated as a part of Indian history, especially in Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Maldeo Rathore**
 
 
• Maldeo Rathore was the ruler of Marwar (Jodhpur) during the 16th century and one of the most powerful Rajput kings of his time.
 
• He successfully resisted attacks from Sher Shah Suri, who described Maldeo as a formidable foe.
 
• While Maldeo Rathore played a significant role in Rajput history, he was not involved in the Battle of Haldighati.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Haldighati - An Overview**
 
 
• The battle is remembered as a symbol of Rajput valor and determination to resist foreign domination.
 
• Despite being outnumbered, Maharana Pratap's forces showcased remarkable bravery and strategy.
 
• The Mughal army eventually gained control of the battlefield, but Maharana Pratap continued his resistance from the forests and hills of Mewar.
 
• This battle is an iconic example of the struggle for independence and the courage of regional leaders against imperial forces.

questions.question: The government's policy of using taxation and public spending to influence the economy is known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fiscal Policy refers to the government's strategy of managing public finances through taxation and public spending to influence the economy.
 
• It is a vital tool for achieving macroeconomic objectives such as economic growth, employment generation, and price stability.
 
• Fiscal Policy is divided into two types: **expansionary fiscal policy** (increased government spending or reduced taxes) and **contractionary fiscal policy** (reduced government spending or increased taxes).
 
• Key instruments of Fiscal Policy include **taxation, government expenditure, subsidies, and public borrowing**.
 
• By adjusting fiscal measures, the government can influence aggregate demand, investment, and consumption patterns in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incomes Policy:**

 
 
• Incomes Policy refers to measures taken by the government to control inflation by restraining wage and price increases.
 
• It is often implemented during periods of high inflation to stabilize the economy.
 
• Examples include wage freezes, price caps, or wage and price guidelines.
 
• Unlike fiscal policy, incomes policy directly influences pricing and wage-setting mechanisms rather than overall public spending and taxation.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Policy:**
 
 
• Industrial Policy involves strategies and measures adopted by the government to promote industrial growth and development.
 
• It focuses on improving infrastructure, providing subsidies, and encouraging private sector investment in industries.
 
• Industrial Policy can include incentives for certain sectors, establishing industrial parks, and promoting innovation and technology adoption.
 
• Its scope is limited to fostering industrial growth, whereas fiscal policy has a broader impact on the overall economy.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Policy:**
 
 
• Regulatory Policy refers to rules and regulations imposed by the government to ensure fair practices, competition, and consumer protection.
 
• It covers areas such as environmental regulations, financial market oversight, and labor laws.
 
• Regulatory policies are designed to prevent monopolies, reduce externalities, and ensure compliance with standards.
 
• Unlike fiscal policy, regulatory policy does not deal with taxation or public spending but focuses on legal frameworks and enforcement.

questions.question: A folk dance known for using "Ghumar" as a primary step, characterized by graceful circular movements and performed predominantly by women during festivities, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthani folk dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghoomar** is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, predominantly performed by women during auspicious occasions and festivals.
 
• The name "Ghoomar" is derived from the Hindi word "Ghoomna," which refers to the circular or spinning movements of the dancers.
 
• Women wear **traditional attire, such as ghagra-choli and odhani,** adorned with intricate embroidery and mirror work, while performing this dance.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional Rajasthani folk songs and instruments like the dhol and nagada, adding a rhythmic element to the performance.
 
• Ghoomar represents Rajasthan’s rich cultural heritage and is performed as a symbol of happiness and celebration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu:**

 
 
• Bihu is the traditional folk dance of Assam, performed during the Rongali Bihu festival, which marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• Dancers wear traditional Assamese attire, such as mekhela chador, and perform to the tunes of traditional instruments like the dhol, pepa, and gogona.
 
• Bihu dance is characterized by quick hand movements, energetic footwork, and expressions of joy and festivity.
 
 
 
• **Chhau:**
 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form originating from eastern India, particularly in Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• It blends elements of martial arts, storytelling, and folk traditions, often depicting mythological themes and epics.
 
• Chhau dancers wear elaborate masks and perform acrobatic movements to the beats of traditional instruments like the dhol and shehnai.
 
 
 
• **Pung Cholam:**
 
 
• Pung Cholam is a traditional dance form of Manipur, performed as an accompaniment to the Manipuri classical dance.
 
• Dancers play the pung (a traditional drum) while performing acrobatic and rhythmic movements.
 
• This dance form is known for its combination of drumming skills and physical agility, symbolizing the vibrant culture of Manipur.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dance as a Theme:**
 
 
• India is home to a diverse range of folk dances, each representing the unique culture, traditions, and heritage of a specific region.

• It emphasizes the importance of early childhood education and aims to bridge gaps in basic literacy and numeracy among children in India.

questions.question: The seminal magical realism work 'One Hundred Years of Solitude', which depicts the Buendía family across generations in Macondo, was penned by which author?

__
 
• **Gabriel García Márquez**, a Colombian novelist, is renowned as one of the most significant authors of the 20th century and a pioneer of magical realism.
 
• His seminal novel, **'One Hundred Years of Solitude'**, was published in 1967 and is regarded as a masterpiece of world literature.
 
• The book chronicles the rise and fall of the Buendía family in the fictional town of Macondo, blending **myth, history, and reality** through the lens of magical realism.
 
• García Márquez won the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982** for his outstanding contribution to literature, especially for works such as 'One Hundred Years of Solitude.'
 
• He played a pivotal role in shaping the **Latin American literary boom** of the 1960s and 1970s, bringing global attention to Latin American literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Mario Vargas Llosa is a Peruvian author and Nobel Prize laureate (2010) known for his contributions to modern Latin American literature.
 
• His notable works include **'The Time of the Hero'** and **'Conversation in the Cathedral.'**
 
• Unlike García Márquez, his style is more grounded in realism rather than magical realism.
 
 
 
• **Julio Cortázar**
 
 
• An Argentine writer, Cortázar is celebrated for his innovative narrative techniques and experimental literature.
 
• His most famous work is **'Hopscotch'** (1963), a novel that allows readers to choose different sequences of chapters to create unique interpretations.
 
• He is often associated with surrealist and avant-garde influences, rather than magical realism.

• Although a prominent figure in Latin American literature, his style is distinct from García Márquez’s magical realism, leaning more towards historical and social commentary.
 
 
 
• **Magical Realism**

• It originated in Latin America and was popularized by authors like Gabriel García Márquez, Isabel Allende, and Jorge Luis Borges.
 
• The genre often reflects cultural, political, and historical realities in an unconventional manner, making it a powerful medium for storytelling.

questions.question: The Northern Plains region is primarily known for the prevalence of which soil type?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alluvial soil is the most prominent soil type found in the Northern Plains of India, covering states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• It is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries over thousands of years.
 
• This soil is highly fertile and rich in essential nutrients like potash, phosphoric acid, and lime, making it ideal for growing crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and oilseeds.
 
• Alluvial soil is stratified, with newer alluvium called Khadar (more fertile) and older alluvium called Bhangar (less fertile) present in the region.
 
• The texture of alluvial soil varies from sandy loam to clay, and it has good water retention capacity, which supports agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forest Soil**

 
 
• Forest soil is found in hilly and mountainous regions covered with forests, such as the Himalayan region.
 
• It is rich in organic matter due to the decomposition of leaves and forest litter, but it may lack essential nutrients for agriculture.
 
• Forest soil is suitable for growing tea, coffee, spices, and tropical fruits in regions like Kerala, Assam, and Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Desert Soil**
 
 
• Desert soil is found in arid and semi-arid regions like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Haryana.
 
• This soil is sandy, saline, and low in organic matter, making it less fertile.
 
• With irrigation, it can support crops like bajra, jowar, and pulses in arid regions.
 
 
 
• **Saline Soil**
 
 
• Saline soil is found in regions with high salt content due to poor drainage or saline water intrusion, such as parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan, and coastal areas.
 
• It is infertile and unsuitable for most crops unless treated to remove excess salts.

questions.question: Dyarchy in provincial governments and expanded Indian participation in governance were introduced by the reforms of the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919, is also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• It introduced the system of Dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces, dividing subjects into Reserved and Transferred categories.
 
• The Reserved subjects, such as law and order, were under the control of the Governor and his Executive Council, while Transferred subjects, like education and public health, were managed by Indian ministers responsible to the legislative council.
 
• This Act marked a significant step toward increased Indian participation in governance, as it expanded the scope of elected representatives in legislative councils.
 
• It also provided for a bicameral legislature at the central level for the first time, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt's India Act, 1784**

 
 
• The Pitt's India Act was passed to address issues of corruption and inefficiency in the East India Company's administration.
 
• It established a Board of Control in Britain to oversee the Company's civil, military, and revenue affairs.
 
• This Act marked the beginning of British government intervention in Indian affairs.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act, 1833**
 
 
• The Charter Act of 1833 centralized administration in India by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
 
• It marked the end of the commercial activities of the East India Company, transforming it into an administrative body.
 
• It also sought to open civil services to Indians, though this was largely ineffective due to discriminatory barriers.
 
 
 
• **Cripps Mission, 1942**
 
 
• The Cripps Mission was sent to India during World War II to gain Indian support for the war effort.
 
• It proposed granting Dominion Status to India after the war and allowing provinces to opt out of the Indian Union.
 
• The proposals were rejected by Indian leaders, leading to the launch of the Quit India Movement by the Congress.

• The court emphasized the importance of transparency, accountability, and protection of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 21 (Right to Life) and 22 (Protection against arbitrary arrest) of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: Which architectural style is famously associated with the Ajanta caves, known for their rock-cut monasteries, chaitya halls, and intricate mural paintings, dating back to the 2nd-6th centuries CE?

__

• These caves were excavated between the **2nd century BCE and the 6th century CE** and served as monasteries, prayer halls (chaityas), and spaces for meditation.
 
• The Ajanta caves are particularly famous for their **intricate mural paintings**, which depict scenes from the Jataka tales and the life of the Buddha.
 
• The caves include impressive chaitya halls (prayer halls) and viharas (monasteries), showcasing a blend of religious functions and aesthetic excellence.
 
• This architectural style reflects the flourishing Buddhist culture in ancient India and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its historical and artistic significance.

• Famous examples include the Chennakesava Temple at Belur and the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.

• **Kalinga temple architecture**
 
 
• This style was predominant in Odisha and parts of Eastern India between the 6th and 13th centuries CE.
 
• It is marked by towering spires (shikhara), intricately carved exteriors, and the use of sandstone and laterite.
 
• Prominent examples include the Sun Temple at Konark and the Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar.
 
• It is primarily associated with Hindu temple architecture and not related to rock-cut structures.

• The "One Belt One Road" (OBOR) initiative, now referred to as the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), is a **global infrastructure and economic development strategy** initiated by China in 2013.
 
• It aims to connect Asia, Europe, and Africa through a network of land and maritime routes to promote **regional trade and economic integration**.
 
• The OBOR project includes two main components: the **Silk Road Economic Belt** (land-based route) and the **21st Century Maritime Silk Road** (sea-based route).

• **Germany**
 
 
• Germany, as a leading European economy, has engaged with the BRI on a limited scale but has raised concerns about China's economic dominance.
 
• It promotes its own initiatives under the European Union's **Global Gateway**, an alternative to the OBOR, focusing on sustainable and transparent global infrastructure development.

• **France**

• Despite criticisms, OBOR continues to play a significant role in shaping the global economic and infrastructural landscape.

questions.question: When is the Hindustani classical Raga Shankara, known for its meditative and devotional mood, traditionally performed?

__
 
• Raga Shankara is a Hindustani classical raga associated with the **nighttime**, specifically the late-night hours.
 
• It is traditionally performed during the **second quarter of the night**, which is around midnight.
 
• Raga Shankara is known for its **devotional and meditative mood**, often invoking feelings of peace and spirituality.
 
• This raga belongs to the **Bilawal Thaat** and uses specific notes (swaras) that emphasize its serene and introspective nature.
 
• It is commonly performed in dhrupad and khyal styles, and its alap and taans are designed to highlight its contemplative essence.

• Morning ragas are generally associated with freshness, energy, and the beginning of a new day.
 
• Examples of morning ragas include Raga Bhairav and Raga Todi, which are known for their calm and serene characteristics.
 
• Morning ragas often emphasize the notes Re (Rishabh) and Dha (Dhaivat) to create a peaceful mood.
 
 
 
• **Afternoon:**
 
 
• Afternoon ragas are performed during the midday and are characterized by a sense of stability and balance.
 
• Examples include Raga Multani and Raga Patdeep, which convey a mood of contemplation and introspection.
 
• These ragas typically use specific note combinations to reflect the heat and stillness of the afternoon.
 
 
 
• **Evening:**

• Prominent evening ragas include Raga Yaman and Raga Marwa, which evoke a sense of romance and tranquility.
 
• These ragas often highlight the notes Ga (Gandhar) and Ni (Nishad) to create a soothing mood.
 
 
 
• **Ragas and Time Theory:**
 
 
• In Hindustani classical music, the **time theory** of ragas associates specific ragas with particular times of the day to evoke the desired emotional response.
 
• This tradition emphasizes the connection between music, natural cycles, and human emotions.
 
• Raga Shankara, being a night raga, is specifically designed to resonate with the calm and introspective atmosphere of the late night.

questions.question: In plant cells, the cytoplasmic channels allowing communication and transport between adjacent cells are formed by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodesmata** are microscopic cytoplasmic channels that connect adjacent plant cells, facilitating communication and the transport of substances.
 
• They allow the exchange of molecules like nutrients, ions, and signaling compounds, ensuring coordination between plant cells.
 
• Plasmodesmata are formed during cell division, remaining as connections between the daughter cells.
 
• Their structure includes a narrow tube-like extension of the endoplasmic reticulum, called the desmotubule, surrounded by cytoplasmic sleeves.
 
• These channels are essential for maintaining plant tissue integrity and coordinating developmental and physiological processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adherens Junctions**

 
 
• These are cell-cell junctions found in animal cells that connect the actin cytoskeleton of adjacent cells.
 
• They help maintain the structural integrity of tissues and play a role in cell signaling and tissue morphogenesis.
 
• Adherens junctions are composed of cadherin proteins that link to actin filaments via catenins.
 
 
 
• **Hemidesmosomes**
 
 
• These are specialized junctions found in animal cells that anchor epithelial cells to the basement membrane.
 
• They contain integrin proteins that connect the intermediate filaments of cells to extracellular matrix components like laminin.
 
• Hemidesmosomes provide mechanical stability to tissues, especially under stress.
 
 
 
• **Septate Junctions**
 
 
• These are cell-cell junctions found in invertebrates, functioning similarly to tight junctions in vertebrates.
 
• They form a barrier to regulate the movement of molecules between cells, maintaining tissue compartmentalization.
 
• Septate junctions are commonly found in epithelial tissues of insects and other arthropods.

• Under the law, pronouncing 'talaq' three times in any form—spoken, written, or electronic—is punishable with up to **3 years of imprisonment** and a fine.

• The Supreme Court later declared the practice of instant triple talaq unconstitutional in the **Shayara Bano case (2017).**
 
 
 
• **2021**

• However, by this time, the 2019 law against triple talaq was already in effect, ensuring legal protection for Muslim women.
 
 
 
• **2022**
 
 
• No significant developments related to triple talaq occurred in 2022.
 
• The law banning triple talaq, enacted in 2019, continued to be implemented across the country.
 
 
 
• **Theme of the Question**
 
 
• Triple talaq, also known as **talaq-e-biddat**, was a practice under Islamic law where a Muslim man could divorce his wife by uttering the word 'talaq' three times.
 
• It was widely criticized for being arbitrary and discriminatory against women, leading to its eventual ban through the **Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.**

questions.question: Intense thunderstorms, marked by lightning, thunder, and heavy rainfall, are predominantly formed by which type of cloud?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cumulonimbus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cumulonimbus clouds** are large, towering clouds that are associated with severe weather phenomena like thunderstorms, lightning, and heavy rainfall.
 
• These clouds form due to the rapid upward movement of warm, moist air, which cools and condenses at higher altitudes, creating towering structures.
 
• Cumulonimbus clouds can reach altitudes of up to 12-20 kilometers and often have a characteristic anvil-shaped top caused by high-altitude winds spreading the cloud horizontally.
 
• They are known to produce extreme weather conditions, including hail, tornadoes, and flash floods, making them one of the most dangerous cloud types.
 
• These clouds are typically found in unstable atmospheric conditions, where warm air near the surface rises rapidly through cooler air above.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nimbostratus Clouds**

 
 
• Nimbostratus clouds are thick, uniform layers of gray clouds that cover the sky and are associated with steady, prolonged rainfall or snowfall rather than intense thunderstorms.
 
• These clouds are typically found in stable atmospheric conditions and do not produce lightning or thunder.
 
 
 
• **Cumulus Clouds**
 
 
• Cumulus clouds are puffy, white clouds with flat bases that often appear in fair weather conditions.
 
• While they can develop into cumulonimbus clouds under the right conditions, they are generally not associated with severe weather on their own.
 
 
 
• **Stratocumulus Clouds**
 
 
• Stratocumulus clouds are low-altitude clouds that appear as large, dark, rounded masses or rolls, often covering the sky in patches.
 
• These clouds typically produce light precipitation, such as drizzle, but are not linked to thunderstorms or intense rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Theme of the Question**
 
 
• Thunderstorms are intense weather phenomena caused by the rapid upward movement of warm, moist air, resulting in condensation and the formation of towering clouds.
 
• The type of cloud formed depends on atmospheric conditions, with cumulonimbus being the most common cloud type associated with severe thunderstorms.

questions.question: The largest organ in the human body, recognized for its functions as a protective barrier, in regulating body temperature, and preventing water loss, is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The skin is the **largest organ in the human body**, with an average surface area of about 1.5 to 2 square meters in adults.
 
• It functions as a **protective barrier** against environmental hazards such as pathogens, harmful substances, and UV radiation.
 
• The skin plays a vital role in **thermoregulation**, helping to maintain body temperature through processes like sweating and vasodilation.
 
• It prevents **water loss** by acting as a semi-permeable membrane, ensuring proper hydration and electrolyte balance.
 
• The skin also serves as a sensory organ, detecting **temperature, pressure, pain, and touch** through specialized nerve endings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lungs:**

 
 
• The lungs are vital organs of the respiratory system, responsible for the **exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide** during breathing.
 
• They are not classified as the largest organ but are essential for maintaining proper oxygen levels in the blood.
 
• Human lungs have a spongy texture and contain millions of alveoli, which facilitate gas exchange.
 
• The lungs also help regulate the body's pH balance by controlling the levels of carbon dioxide in the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Kidneys:**
 
 
• The kidneys are bean-shaped organs in the urinary system, primarily responsible for **filtering waste products** and excess substances from the blood.
 
• They maintain the body's electrolyte balance and regulate blood pressure through the production of hormones like renin.
 
• Kidneys also play a crucial role in the production of red blood cells by secreting erythropoietin.
 
• While critical for bodily functions, they are not the largest organ in the human body.
 
 
 
• **Stomach:**
 
 
• The stomach is a muscular organ in the digestive system that facilitates the **breakdown of food** through mechanical and chemical digestion.
 
• It secretes gastric juices, including hydrochloric acid and pepsin, to digest proteins.
 
• The stomach is essential for nutrient absorption but is much smaller in size compared to the skin.
 
• It also plays a role in immunity by killing harmful bacteria with its acidic environment.
 
 
 
• **Human Body and Organ Systems:**
 
 
• The human body consists of multiple organ systems working together to sustain life, including the circulatory, respiratory, digestive, and integumentary systems.
 
• The **integumentary system**, which includes the skin, hair, nails, and glands, is the most visible system and serves as the body's first line of defense.
 
• Each organ system has specialized functions, demonstrating the complexity and interdependence of human anatomy.

questions.question: The gas primarily responsible for trapping infrared radiation in Earth's atmosphere, leading to the greenhouse effect and global warming, is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a greenhouse gas that absorbs and traps infrared radiation, contributing significantly to the greenhouse effect and global warming.
 
• Its concentration in Earth's atmosphere has increased due to human activities like burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes.
 
• CO₂ has a long atmospheric lifetime, meaning it remains in the atmosphere for decades to centuries, amplifying its warming effects.
 
• It is responsible for approximately 76% of global greenhouse gas emissions, according to the IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change).
 
• Efforts to mitigate global warming focus on reducing CO₂ emissions through renewable energy adoption, afforestation, and carbon capture technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Helium**

 
 
• Helium is an inert gas and does not absorb infrared radiation, meaning it does not contribute to the greenhouse effect.
 
• It is primarily used in applications like cryogenics, gas chromatography, and as a cooling medium in nuclear reactors.
 
• Helium is non-reactive and does not interact with other gases or compounds in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Neon**
 
 
• Neon is a noble gas and is not involved in the greenhouse effect as it does not trap heat or absorb infrared radiation.
 
• It is most commonly used in lighting applications, such as neon signs, and in high-voltage indicators.
 
• Neon does not contribute to global warming or atmospheric changes as it is chemically inert.
 
 
 
• **Krypton**
 
 
• Krypton is another noble gas that does not absorb infrared radiation and thus does not contribute to the greenhouse effect.
 
• It is used in applications like lighting (fluorescent lamps) and photography.
 
• Krypton remains stable and inert in the atmosphere and has no significant impact on climate change.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect**
 
 
• The greenhouse effect is a natural process that warms Earth's surface by trapping heat from the Sun through greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor.
 
• While the greenhouse effect is essential for maintaining life on Earth, excessive emissions of greenhouse gases lead to global warming and climate change.
 
• Reducing greenhouse gas emissions and adopting sustainable practices are crucial to mitigating its adverse effects on the planet.

questions.question: Blood vessels in humans that contain valves to prevent backflow of blood and ensure unidirectional circulation toward the heart are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Veins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Veins are blood vessels** responsible for carrying deoxygenated blood from various parts of the body back to the heart, except for the pulmonary vein, which carries oxygenated blood.
 
• Unlike arteries, veins have **valves** that prevent the backflow of blood and ensure unidirectional circulation toward the heart.
 
• Veins are thinner and less elastic compared to arteries as they experience lower blood pressure.
 
• Some examples of veins include the **jugular vein, vena cava, and femoral vein**, which play crucial roles in systemic circulation.
 
• Veins rely on the contraction of skeletal muscles to help push blood back to the heart, overcoming gravity, especially in the lower limbs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arterioles**:

 
 
• Arterioles are small branches of arteries that lead to capillaries.
 
• They play a vital role in regulating blood flow and pressure through vasoconstriction and vasodilation.
 
• Unlike veins, arterioles do not have valves, as they carry blood away from the heart under higher pressure.
 
• These vessels are lined with smooth muscle that controls their diameter.
 
 
 
• **Venules**:
 
 
• Venules are small vessels that collect blood from capillaries and transport it to larger veins.
 
• They are part of the venous system but differ from veins in size and structure.
 
• Venules do not have valves like veins, as they are located closer to the capillary beds.
 
• These vessels are essential in the exchange of nutrients and waste products between blood and tissues.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Artery**:
 
 
• The pulmonary artery is a unique artery that carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs for oxygenation.
 
• It is part of the pulmonary circulation, which is distinct from systemic circulation.
 
• Unlike veins, arteries generally do not have valves, as blood flows under high pressure away from the heart.
 
• The pulmonary artery is divided into left and right branches, each serving one lung.
 
 
 
• **Valves in Circulation:**
 
 
• The presence of valves is a distinctive feature of veins, ensuring the proper return of blood to the heart.
 
• Valves are especially prominent in the veins of the lower limbs to counteract gravity.
 
• Other blood vessels like arteries, arterioles, and capillaries lack valves due to their different structural and functional roles.

• The eight ministers included the following roles: Peshwa (Prime Minister), Amatya (Finance Minister), Sachiv (Secretary), Mantri (Interior Minister), Senapati (Commander-in-Chief), Sumant (Foreign Affairs Minister), Panditrao (Religious Head), and Nyayadhish (Chief Justice).
 
• The Ashtapradhan was a unique administrative structure introduced by Shivaji to centralize power and improve the efficiency of the Maratha Empire during the 17th century.
 
• This system was inspired by ancient Indian administrative practices and was tailored to suit the needs of the Maratha state, ensuring accountability and specialization within the government.

• **Mahasabha**
 
 
• The Mahasabha was a term used in ancient and medieval India to denote a general assembly or council, often at the village or community level.
 
• It was primarily associated with local self-governance in ancient Indian administrative systems, particularly in South India.
 
• Shivaji’s centralized administrative system, represented by the Ashtapradhan, was distinct from the decentralized functioning of Mahasabhas.

questions.question: Which hormone, secreted by the pineal gland, primarily regulates the sleep-wake cycle, also known as the circadian rhythm, in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Melatonin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Melatonin** is a hormone produced by the pineal gland, located in the brain.
 
• It primarily regulates the sleep-wake cycle or circadian rhythm by responding to light and darkness.
 
• Its secretion increases during the evening, signaling the body to prepare for sleep, and decreases in the morning to promote wakefulness.
 
• Melatonin influences various physiological functions, including mood regulation, immune system modulation, and antioxidant activity.
 
• Disruption of melatonin production due to factors like excessive screen time or irregular sleep patterns can lead to sleep disorders and affect overall health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Insulin:**

 
 
• Insulin is a hormone produced by the pancreas that regulates blood glucose levels.
 
• It facilitates the uptake of glucose into cells for energy production or storage as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
 
• Insulin dysfunction is associated with conditions like diabetes mellitus.
 
 
 
• **Estrogen:**
 
 
• Estrogen is a group of hormones responsible for the development and regulation of the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• It is primarily produced by the ovaries, with smaller amounts secreted by the adrenal glands and fat tissues.
 
• Estrogen also plays a role in bone health, cardiovascular function, and maintaining skin elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Growth Hormone:**
 
 
• Also known as somatotropin, growth hormone is produced by the anterior pituitary gland.
 
• It stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and regeneration in humans and other animals.
 
• Deficiency of growth hormone can lead to stunted growth, while excess levels can cause gigantism or acromegaly.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme:**
 
 
• The question revolves around the role of hormones in regulating physiological processes.
 
• Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands, which coordinate various functions in the body.
 
• Each hormone has a specific role, ranging from metabolic regulation to development and sleep-wake cycles.
